Chapter 0390 BPMOUTPUT

The Wire Choir

The right song, at the right moment, out of somebody else's window.

Look up in an East Van lane: telephone poles, layers of wires, trolley lines, transformers. Add every radio, every car stereo, every pair of headphones and the bass leaking under a warehouse door, and you have the Wire Choir. It is how Terminal City sings to itself.

When a neighbourhood goes quiet, the Choir leans on coincidence. Somebody's car at a red light is playing the exact song. A band is rehearsing through a wall you happen to be leaning on. A radio in an upstairs apartment, a window left open, a snatch of something from a loading bay at two in the morning. You still choose what you listen to. You really did. The timing was just a little too good.

It cannot reach everywhere. Inside Stanley Park the signal fades into the trees. And whatever people make out of what they heard, a track, a night out, a wall of paint, comes back into the wires and keeps the city from falling silent. No one hears the broadcast as an announcement.

The ruleNo one hears the broadcast as an announcement.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented.
